messages:
jamie: quick heads-up — saw a jump in unique span attrs in prod ingest this morning, looks like request_id + prompt content explosion. raw counts spiking in the 99th percentile. anyone else seeing this?

olivia: yup saw it on the per-tenant dashboard. top contributors are `http.request_id`, `user.id` and `prompt.hash` variants.

sam: we should avoid storing raw request ids. proposal: deterministic bucketing of request_id -> 100 buckets, store bucket id and a salted short hash (8 chars) instead of full id. keeps cardinality bounded and supports stable sampling.

jamie: agree. algorithm sketch: `bucket = (hash(salt + request_id) mod 100)` then `short = hex(hash(salt + request_id))[:8]`. store `hc.bucket=xx` and `hc.id=short`. no mapping kept.

tia: sounds ok, but we need to think about salt rotation and cross-service consistency. if different services use different salts we lose the ability to correlate.

sam: plan: make salt an environment config per deployment tier (prod-global-salt v1). rotation policy: rotate every 90 days, keep last 2 salts for overlap. we include `hc.salt_version` attr so older spans remain interpretable for aggregation.

ryan: what about user IDs? some customers pass email-like ids. we should treat `user.id` same as request_id, but with an extra rule: if it matches known UUID pattern, we bucket; if it looks like an email we hash+truncate and mark `attr.redacted=email`.

mona: question: for the console and dashboards, do we want the bucket numbers to be visible? i.e., will product teams query `hc.bucket`?

jamie: yes — expose bucket as a stable dimension in analytics. add an aggregation helper in the console that shows top buckets and anonymized samples (only `hc.id` prefixes). no raw IDs.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: telemetry-ingest/enable-hc-buckets v1 -> staging at 01:15 UTC.

tia: another edge: prompt hashes. we already compute `prompt_hash` for quality monitoring but some apps include user PII in prompts. we should treat prompt_hash similarly but also apply entropy thresholding before storing. if prompt content entropy > X then only store bucket, else store short hash.

sam: pseudo rule for ingest:
```
if attr_name in ["http.request_id", "user.id"]:
  hc_full = H(salt + value)
  store hc.bucket = hc_full % 100
  store hc.id = hex(hc_full)[:8]
elif attr_name == "prompt_text":
  ph = sha256(prompt_text)
  if shannon_entropy(prompt_text) > 4.5:
    store prompt_bucket = ph % 50
  else:
    store prompt_hash = hex(ph)[:8]
```

olivia: also add sampling tag `hc.sampled=true` when we keep a full-ish representation in short-hash mode, otherwise `hc.sampled=false`. helps downstream eval tooling.

ryan: retention: full telemetry (with short hashes) -> 90d, high-cardinality aggregates only -> 2y. raw attribute values must be purged immediately unless explicitly whitelisted.

mona: need docs + SDK change: instrumentations must call `telemetry.scrub(attrs)` helper before export. we'll add a small compatibility shim so older SDKs fallback to ingest-side scrub.

jamie: ops checklist before deploy: 1) add salt config + version header to traces 2) implement bucketing + truncation 3) update console to hide raw attrs 4) add sampling flags to exported spans 5) run a 48h shadow deploy and compare counts.

tia: one more: for canary rollouts, keep a debug toggle to preserve full ids for 24h per team and auto-expire. require explicit approval (security) and log who enabled.

sam: I'll open the RFC PR with the policy + code snippets and a small k8s config for salt rotation.

jamie: perfect. thanks all — tagging @ryan @olivia for the console/backfill impacts. :thumbsup:
